body:
## Summary

- backfill all 22 tagged versions that lacked GitHub Release objects
- add a fail-closed Rust reconciliation script that compares default-branch version tags with GitHub Releases
- run reconciliation immediately after release creation and in a separate daily scheduled workflow
- exercise both the workflow wiring and order-independent set comparison in automated tests

## Root cause

The release pipeline had static tests for job ordering, but no runtime assertion that a tag received a GitHub Release. A cancelled or skipped release step could therefore leave crates and tags published while CI stayed silent about the missing Release object.

## Reproduction

Before the backfill, the repository had 50 version tags and 28 GitHub Releases. Comparing default-branch tags against `gh release list` produced 22 missing tags. The new `reports_every_tag_without_a_release` unit test captures that missing-set behavior, including semantic versions whose lexical order differs.

## Verification

- all 22 missing Releases were recreated from their matching `CHANGELOG.md` sections
- live reconciliation reports 51 default-branch version tags and 51 GitHub Releases (including the subsequently published v0.53.0)
- `cargo test --locked --all-features --verbose`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --locked --no-deps --all-features`
- `cargo package --locked --list`
- `rust-script --test scripts/check-github-releases.rs`
- release workflow invariant and file-size scripts
- `actionlint -no-color .github/workflows/release.yml .github/workflows/verify-releases.yml`
- `npm audit --audit-level=high --prefix ui`

## Historical note

The crates.io API currently returns 49 package versions and does not return `0.24.0`, despite the issue describing all 22 tags as published crates. `v0.24.0` still has a repository tag and a full changelog section, so it was included in the requested tag-to-Release backfill.

Fixes #118
title: fix(ci): detect missing GitHub releases
